about: Washington state calls with their own application windows that FundHubWA leaves out, entered by hand from each program's own page: Department of Commerce social service and capital grants, Office of Crime Victims Advocacy funding, and ArtsWA grants. Also King County programs. grantmatch/local.py checks this file and turns each entry into a Washington program record; the weekly page watcher rereads every page. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

programs.title: WorkFirst Service Providers
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Community Jobs program
programs.objectives: Contracts to run transitional and community-based work experience programs for WorkFirst (TANF) recipients: intensive case management, career development, subsidized employment and related supports. Commerce will award 27 contracts statewide, one for each WorkFirst service area, for July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2029.
programs.who: Community-based organizations, one per WorkFirst service area. The request for proposals and its application materials on the page give the full eligibility rules.
programs.application: Download the RFP and application materials from the page. Optional pre-proposal conference December 3, 2026, 2 p.m. PT on Zoom; optional statement of intent by December 17, 2026; questions until December 23, 2026.
programs.award: 27 contracts, one per WorkFirst service area. Contract amounts are in the RFP.
programs.deadlines: Proposals due Thursday, January 14, 2027, by 3 p.m. PT.
programs.subjects: Employment; Job training; Case management; TANF; Poverty; Families

programs.title: Behavioral Health Facilities Closure Prevention
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Behavioral Health Facilities program
programs.objectives: Capital grants to keep licensed, operating behavioral health facilities open: physical repairs and upgrades, capital maintenance needed for licensing, and capital improvements that free up cash for operations. Funds may not be used for expansion. The facility must be at significant risk of closing within two years without the state's help.
programs.who: Nonprofits, for-profit businesses, public entities, tribes and Indian health care providers, community hospitals and community-based behavioral health providers, for licensed, operating facilities. Some enhanced services facilities and assisted living facilities with DSHS licenses and contracts also qualify.
programs.application: Complete the eligibility screening, then apply through ZoomGrants. A recorded webinar from November 5, 2026 is on the page. Grantees must keep the facility in its contracted use for at least 10 years.
programs.award: $9.7 million in all, first come, first served until it runs out. Funds must be spent by June 30, 2027.
programs.deadlines: Open from October 23, 2026 until midnight June 30, 2027, or until the money runs out, whichever comes first.
programs.subjects: Behavioral health; Mental health; Substance use; Facilities; Capital

programs.title: Building Communities Fund
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Community Capital Facilities
programs.objectives: Capital grants to buy, build or renovate non-residential community and social service centers, to expand access to services in communities with the greatest need. Reimburses 25% of eligible project costs. Operating costs aren't eligible.
programs.who: Nonprofit organizations and tribes registered in Washington, for projects that serve a distressed community or a substantial number of low-income or disadvantaged people.
programs.application: Pass the eligibility test, then apply through ZoomGrants. Commerce holds application workshops when a round opens.
programs.award: Reimburses 25% of eligible project costs. The 2027-2029 round set no minimum or maximum award.
programs.deadlines: A competitive round every two years. The 2027-2029 round closed August 20, 2026. Watch the page for the next round.
programs.subjects: Capital; Facilities; Community centers; Social services

programs.title: Youth Recreational Facilities
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Community Capital Facilities
programs.objectives: Capital grants for buying, building or substantially renovating non-residential youth recreational facilities, paying up to 25% of eligible capital costs. Operating costs aren't eligible.
programs.who: Nonprofit organizations and tribes registered in Washington, with a legally constituted board, dedicated to youth activities. Facilities offer supervised recreation for youth with an educational or social service part.
programs.application: Apply through ZoomGrants when a round opens. The Youth Recreational Facilities Board reviews applications and recommends projects.
programs.award: Up to 25% of eligible capital costs, and no more than $1,200,000.
programs.deadlines: A competitive round every two years. The 2027-2029 round closed May 28, 2026. Watch the page for the next round.

programs.title: Building for the Arts
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Community Capital Facilities
programs.objectives: Capital grants for buying, building or substantially renovating facilities for performing arts, art museum and cultural organizations, paying as much as 33% of eligible project costs. Operating costs aren't eligible.
programs.who: Nonprofit performing arts, art museum and cultural organizations, and tribes, registered in Washington with a legally constituted board.
programs.application: Apply through ZoomGrants when a round opens; Commerce posts funding guidelines and holds a workshop first.
programs.award: Up to 33% of eligible project costs, and no more than $2,000,000.
programs.deadlines: A competitive round every two years. The 2027-2029 round closed July 9, 2026. Watch the page for the next round.

programs.title: Crime Victim Services Grants
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Office of Crime Victims Advocacy (OCVA)
programs.objectives: Direct and competitive grants to organizations across Washington that serve survivors and victims of crime, including federal Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) and STOP funds. OCVA releases requests for proposals throughout the year, many in spring for July 1 starts and in fall for January 1 starts.
programs.who: Each request for proposals names its eligible applicants. Organizations that serve victims apply; the money isn't available to individual victims.
programs.application: Watch the page, or sign up for OCVA's email list there, for each request for proposals. Each one gives its own grant period, amount and how to apply.
programs.award: Set in each request for proposals.
programs.deadlines: Requests for proposals come out through the year, often in spring and fall. None was open when this was checked.
programs.contact: Through the page's sign-up form, or the Commerce contact page
programs.subjects: Crime victims; Domestic violence; Sexual assault; Victim advocacy; Safety

programs.title: Arts in Education Project Grant
programs.objectives: Projects that expand arts learning for preschool and K-12 students in Washington, free of charge for every participating student, with arts learning goals and sequential learning. Covers project staff, educator professional learning, in-state travel, materials (up to 25% of the award) and indirect costs (up to 15%).
programs.who: Washington 501(c)(3) nonprofits with current state nonprofit status and a federal tax-exempt letter, public schools and districts, Educational Service Districts, Head Start and ECEAP programs, and tribal, state or city government agencies, serving Washington students. Fiscally sponsored, for-profit, political or advocacy organizations and individuals can't apply.
programs.application: Apply in Submittable between January 4 and February 11, 2027. Info sessions January 7 and January 21, 2027 at 4 p.m. Nonprofits attach their IRS letter of determination and mission statement.
programs.award: $10,000 to $15,000, no match required. Projects run July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2028.
programs.deadlines: Applications open January 4, 2027 and close February 11, 2027 at 5 p.m.
programs.subjects: Arts; Arts education; Children; Youth; Schools; Early learning

programs.title: Art Project Grant (Grants to Organizations)
programs.objectives: Reimbursement grants for public arts, heritage and culture projects in Washington with a clear start and end inside ArtsWA's fiscal year (July 1 to June 30). Ongoing programs aren't funded.
programs.who: Washington nonprofit organizations registered with the Secretary of State, among the other types the year's guidelines list. Projects must be open to the public and happen in Washington.
programs.application: Apply in Submittable when the year's round opens; the guidelines on the page list who can apply that year.
programs.award: Small project grants paid as reimbursement after expenses. The year's amounts are in its guidelines.
programs.deadlines: Once a year. The FY27 round ran March 9 to April 16, 2026. Watch ArtsWA's grants page for the next round.
programs.contact: ArtsWA Grants to Organizations staff, listed on the page

programs.title: Youth Cannabis and Commercial Tobacco Prevention: Community and Priority Populations Grant
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Health, Youth Cannabis and Commercial Tobacco Prevention Program (YCCTPP)
programs.objectives: Five-year grants for policy, systems and environmental change that prevents youth cannabis and commercial tobacco use and addresses its root causes. A Community Track funds partners working in a geographic region; a Priority Population Track funds partners with culturally specific expertise, trusted relationships and lived experience in the communities most affected.
programs.who: Washington 501(c)(3) nonprofits, community-based organizations, federally recognized tribes and tribal organizations, city governments, local health jurisdictions, other government entities, schools and districts, educational organizations, and coalitions. Groups without 501(c)(3) status can apply with a fiscal sponsor and a signed sponsorship agreement.
programs.application: Apply by the request for applications the Department of Health released September 17, 2026; the announcement page links its Q&A sessions and newsletter.
programs.award: $50,000 to $611,325 a year. Funding runs July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2032. Awards are expected by January 28, 2027.
programs.deadlines: Applications due December 12, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific.
programs.subjects: Youth; Prevention; Substance use; Cannabis; Tobacco; Public health; Community coalitions

programs.title: Capital Project Capacity-Building Grants
programs.agency: Washington State Department of Commerce, Community Capacity Initiative
programs.objectives: Small grants for the critical next step in an early-stage capital project, such as targeted technical assistance and predevelopment work, so organizations are ready to seek capital funding. Priority goes to projects in overburdened communities that address housing, energy or infrastructure needs. Not for construction or land purchase.
programs.who: Washington nonprofits, local governments and federally recognized tribes; each round's request for applications sets the exact rules.
programs.application: Apply with the online form in each round's request for applications. The Community Capacity Initiative also offers free training on capital project readiness.
programs.award: An earlier nonprofit round gave awards of up to $50,000 each.
programs.deadlines: The FY2027 round closed October 30, 2026. Commerce says more opportunities will be posted; watch the page.
programs.subjects: Capital; Capacity building; Predevelopment; Housing; Facilities; Technical assistance

programs.title: Art Projects
programs.objectives: Art projects of any medium shared with King County communities.
programs.who: Individual artists and art groups based in King County. Nonprofit status is not required.
programs.deadlines: Applications are due March 10, 2027, at 5 p.m.
programs.source_note: 4Culture says its posted guidelines describe the previous cycle and will be updated before applications open.

programs.title: Heritage Projects
programs.objectives: Documentation, exhibits and interpretation of heritage and history in King County.
programs.who: King County residents, and organizations, community groups, municipalities, Tribal governments and unincorporated or fiscally sponsored groups located and working in King County.
programs.deadlines: Applications are due March 10, 2027, at 5 p.m.
programs.source_note: 4Culture says its posted guidelines describe the previous cycle and will be updated before applications open.

programs.title: Open 4Culture
programs.objectives: A first 4Culture grant for arts, heritage and historic preservation projects.
programs.who: Individuals, and groups based in King County with an arts, heritage or preservation mission, that are new to 4Culture. Nonprofit status is not required.
programs.application: Applications reopen in April 2027; apply at least three months before the project or event.
programs.deadlines: Applications reopen April 2027, then ongoing, due three months before the event.
programs.source_note: 4Culture says its posted guidelines describe the previous cycle and will be updated before applications open.

programs.title: Building for Equity: Project Development
programs.objectives: Planning and early design for cultural facility projects.
programs.who: King County-based nonprofit arts, cultural, heritage, preservation, science and technology organizations, Tribal governments, public agencies, and cultural or science groups fiscally sponsored by a 501(c)(3).
programs.application: Intent to apply by March 25, 2027, then the final application.
programs.deadlines: Intent to apply due March 25, 2027; final application due April 8, 2027, at 5 p.m.
programs.source_note: 4Culture says its posted guidelines describe the previous cycle and will be updated before applications open.
